client: Dana Okafor, Head of People Ops, Tidewater Biologics (fictional)

notes.transcript: Oh, I like the energy already. This is an opener. Keep this.
notes.production_note: Keep the intro as is; client approves it as the offsite opener.

notes.transcript: 'Two minds in the machine on a single page,' that's good, that's the whole pitch.
notes.production_note: Protect the line 'two minds in the machine on a single page'; it is the pitch leadership will quote.

notes.transcript: Hmm, 'tactical sun' feels a little corny though. I don't know. Something about it.
notes.production_note: Rewrite 'eighty percent under the tactical sun'; the phrase reads as corny. Delivery is fine.
notes.clarifying_question: Is it the words, or the way they're sung?
notes.clarification: The words. The singing's fine, it's 'tactical sun.'

notes.transcript: Yes. That's the line. The chorus has to keep 'ten percent to innovate, the rest to operate,' do not touch that. People need to hear the number twice.
notes.production_note: Keep 'ten percent to innovate, the rest to operate' verbatim; it is the required 80/20 message and should repeat.

notes.transcript: Love the San Diego shout-out. 'Biomedical secrets that the algorithms keep,' legal might flinch at 'secrets.' Not a dealbreaker.
notes.production_note: Swap 'secrets' in verse 3 for a word legal will accept; keep the San Diego reference.

notes.transcript: This verse is long. Feels like the same idea as verse one. Could we cut it or fold it in?
notes.production_note: Trim verse 4 or fold it into verse 1; client hears it as a repeat.

notes.transcript: The Star Trek line is going to land with our CTO. Keep it. The drums get a little busy under here though.
notes.production_note: Keep the Star Trek line; pull the drums back under the bridge.

notes.transcript: Wednesday night doesn't mean anything to us, our offsite is a Thursday. And if we ever say TIDE, it's one word, 'tide,' not T-I-D-E.
notes.production_note: Change 'Wednesday night' to Thursday; note pronunciation: TIDE is said as one word.
